hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
hook.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
hook.line: Even Arjuna, the finest archer alive, froze when the fight was against his own people.
hook.translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
hook.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
alternates.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
alternates.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
alternates.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
alternates.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
alternates.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

alternates.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
alternates.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.

prasang.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.

verse.meaning: Arjuna, the greatest archer in the world, is on a battlefield. He looks at the other side and sees his own kin, his teachers, and his family. He is suddenly filled with grief and pity. He tells Krishna that the sight of his people eager to fight is too much for him. He is overcome. He lets his bow fall to the ground and sits down. The verse says that even the strongest person can freeze when the fight is against their own people. It is not a story of a hero stepping up.
verse.for_you: You are standing in your own waiting room, and the door is shut. The one you are closest to will not listen, and the one you share your life with is fighting. You feel the ground give way. You are not weak for feeling this.
verse.scene_line: You are Arjuna, and the bow has slipped from your hands.
asks: How do I stop the fighting with my partner?
What if I am not strong enough for this?
Why does my teenager not listen to me?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The creation story: the first being, alone.
verse.sanskrit: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥
verse.line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?
verse.translation: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
verse.why: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

prasang.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

verse.meaning: The first being stood alone and felt fear. It asked itself what it was afraid of. It realized there was no one else, so there was nothing to fear. Fear only comes when there is a second. When it understood this, the fear left.
verse.for_you: The unease you feel with your teenager and the fights with your partner come from a second, a separate will you cannot control. The fear is real, but it is not the whole story. The truth is that you are not the problem.
verse.try_today: Notice the exact moment you feel the fear of what might happen, and ask what second is there.
verse.scene_line: You are the first being, alone, asking what you are afraid of.
asks: What second am I afraid of?
How do I stop feeling alone in this fight?
Is my fear the real enemy?

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: After Sita is taken, Lakshman comforts Ram, who is lost in grief.
verse.sanskrit: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥
verse.line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
verse.translation: Take heart, best of men. Which living being does trouble not touch? Troubles strike like fire, king, and pass in a moment.
verse.why: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.

prasang.title: Ram's grief and Lakshman's counsel
prasang.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.
prasang.story_hook: He came back to the hut calling her name, and no one answered.
prasang.lesson: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.

verse.meaning: After Sita is taken, Ram searches the empty forest, questions the trees, and breaks down. He rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman, the steady brother, steps in. He tells Ram to take heart, that trouble touches everyone, flares up like fire, and passes in a moment.
verse.for_you: Your teenager's silence and your partner's anger are the fire flaring up right now. Lakshman is telling you that this heat is not the end of the forest, that it will pass, and that you do not have to burn the whole world down to answer it.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment of the day when the heat drops.
asks: How do I know this fire will pass before I burn out?
Can I trust that the trouble will not last forever?

verse.speaker: Angiras
verse.setting: Angiras on truth as the path.
verse.sanskrit: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाऽऽक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥
verse.line: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. Truth lays the road that the wise walk.
verse.translation: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. By truth the divine path is laid out, by which the sages, their desires fulfilled, travel to where the highest treasure of truth is.
verse.why: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.
verse.misuse: Truth wins in the long run; it is not a promise of quick victory.

prasang.title: Two birds on one tree
prasang.summary: Two birds sit on one tree: one eats the fruit and grieves, the other simply watches. When the anxious bird sees the calm one beside it, its sorrow falls away. The section goes on to praise truth, effort and freedom from craving.
prasang.lesson: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.

verse.for_you: The arguments with your partner and the silence from your teenager are not the whole of you. There is a calm witness inside that simply watches the fire without burning. Let that witness hold the worry about what might happen next. It is enough for now.
verse.try_today: Notice the part of you that simply watches the fighting and the silence.
verse.scene_line: You are the grieving bird on the branch, watching the fire of the argument pass.
asks: How do I find the calm witness when the noise is so loud?

verse.speaker: Lankini
verse.setting: Lanka's gatekeeper, humbled by Hanuman, sends him into the city with a blessing.
verse.sanskrit: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
verse.line: Walk into the hard task carrying what you love in your heart, and even poison turns to nectar.
verse.translation: Enter the city and do all your work, holding the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a one, poison turns to nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean shrinks to a hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
verse.why: Carry what you love into the hard place, and the hard place changes.

prasang.title: Lankini at the gate of Lanka
prasang.summary: Entering Lanka at night as small as a mosquito, Hanuman is caught by Lankini, the city's guardian. One blow of his fist floors her; she remembers a prophecy that this means the city's end, and blesses him: a moment of good company outweighs heaven, and if he carries Ram in his heart, poison will turn to nectar.
prasang.story_hook: The guard at the gate of Lanka caught a mosquito.
prasang.lesson: Carry what you love into the hard place, and the hard place changes.

verse.meaning: Hanuman has just struck down Lankini, the guardian of Lanka. She knows this blow marks the city's end but instead of cursing him, she blesses him. She tells him to enter the city and do his work, but to keep Ram in his heart. When you carry what you love into a dangerous place, the danger changes. The poison becomes nectar, the ocean becomes small, and fire becomes cool.
verse.for_you: Your teenager does not listen, and the fighting with your partner leaves you feeling like you are entering a hard place every day. You do not need to win the fight or force the listening.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the gate of a hard room, carrying what you love in your heart.
asks: What does it mean to carry my love into a hard room?
How can I stop the hard place from changing me?
What if I cannot feel the love right now?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
verse.line: Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
verse.translation: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.
verse.misuse: Surrender is trust, not giving up your judgement or your effort.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen, afraid of the war ahead. Krishna tells him to offer all his action to the divine, to reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear. He says that by taking refuge in this alone, Arjuna will find supreme peace.
verse.for_you: You are caught between the noise of your children and the silence of your partner. You are carrying the fear of what might happen next. You do not have to carry this alone. You can offer your effort to something steady, and let that steadiness hold you.
verse.try_today: Place your hand on your heart and name one thing you love.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the center of your own battlefield, holding what you love.
asks: How do I set down the fear of what might happen?
Where do I find the strength to choose freely today?
What does it look like to offer my action to something steady?

story.title: Father and son go back to school
story.story_hook: When his son came home stumped, Uddalaka did something unusual for a famous teacher.
story.summary: A patron asks young Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer. He asks his father, who admits he does not know either and suggests they both go to the patron as students. Chitra welcomes Uddalaka for his humility.
story.lesson: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.

anchor.speaker: Shvetaketu and Uddalaka Aruni
anchor.setting: A patron asks Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer; he goes to his father.
anchor.sanskrit: स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद हन्ताचार्यं प्रच्छानीति स ह पितरमासाद्य पप्रच्छेतीति स होवाचाहमप्येतन्न वेद सदस्येव वयं स्वाध्यायमधीत्य हरामहे यन्नः परे ददत्येह्युभौ गमिष्याव इति ॥
anchor.line: 'I don't know either,' the father told his son. 'Let's both go and learn, as students.'
anchor.translation: He said, 'I do not know this. Let me ask my teacher.' He went to his father and asked. The father said, 'I too do not know it. We have studied the Veda and take what others give us. Come, let us both go.'
anchor.why: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.
